title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is the second part of the 'équation des lacets' notes, a continuation of La Longue Marche. Grothendieck is comparing two profinite pictures of the 'Teichmüller tower' in low dimension.

- The genus-1 picture is built on M = N_{1,1}^~ ≅ Γ_Q^~·𝔊^+. Here 𝔊^+ is SL(2,Z)^∧ and Γ_Q^~ is his combinatorial substitute for Gal(Q̄/Q), essentially a GT-hat-like group.
- The genus-0 picture is built on M_{0,3}^~.
- On the previous page he defined subgroups of M from the two elliptic generators ρ (order 3/6) and σ (order 2/4):
  - N^*_ρ, N^*_σ are the elements fixing ρ, resp. σ, up to the cyclotomic power ε(u).
  - Z_{ρ,σ} and Z^!_{ρ,σ} are the groups of elements u simultaneously 'normalizing' the pair.
- The two 'canonical fundamental loops' are maps a: Z^! → N^*_ρ/μ and b: Z^! → N^*_σ, with μ = {±1}. They are characterized by the congruences (122): u ≡ b mod Π_0^∧ and u ≡ ε_3[σ]a mod Π^∧.

(123). Composing a and b with the projections δ_ρ, δ_σ onto γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ Π_Q^~ gives a triangle-shaped diagram. The dashed arrow δ_Z is the direct projection Z^! → γ_{ρ,σ}. Implicitly the claim, or the question, is that the diagram commutes.

Correction of p. 594'. He then corrects a confusion made earlier between:
- Z = Z_{ρ,σ}, sitting in M^*_{0,3}^~, and
- Z^! = Z ∩ M^{!~}_{0,3}.

(124)–(125). Both are semidirect ('1/2-direct') products of a 'Galois part' M(0) ≅ Π_Q^~ with a procyclic 'inertia' part L_0:
- Z_{ρ,σ} ≅ M^♮(0)·L_0^𝔊 ⊂ M, which is isomorphic to the analogous group M_{0,3}^{♮~}(0)·L_0^{𝔊_{0,3}} inside M_{0,3}^~.
- Z^!_{ρ,σ} ≅ M(0)·L_0^π, which is isomorphic to M_{0,3}^~(0)·L_0^{π_{0,3}}.

In modern language, these are decomposition-group-type subgroups 'at the cusp' (tangential base point): a semidirect product Ẑ(1) ⋊ Galois. They are identified between the M_{1,1} picture and the M_{0,3} picture.

(126). The two extensions
- 1 → L_0^π → Z^! → γ → 1
- 1 → L_0^𝔊 → Z → γ → 1

are compared by inclusions, with the identity on the quotient γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ M(0) ≅ Π_Q^~.

(127). The kernel inclusion is the index-2 inclusion L_0^π = ℓ_0^{Ẑ} = ε_0^{2Ẑ} ⊂ L_0^𝔊 = ε_0^{Ẑ}. So the loop ℓ_0 in the π-world is the square of the 'half-loop' ε_0 in the 𝔊 = SL_2-world. This is the familiar ±1 / SL_2-versus-PSL_2 phenomenon at the cusp.

Purpose. The next page restricts the homomorphisms of (123) to L_0^π:
- the map to N^*_ρ/{±1} is trivial;
- the map to N^*_σ factors through L_0^π/L_0^{π_0} ≅ μ, sending the generator to −1.

This bookkeeping serves to make the 'équation des lacets' relations precise, including the correct sign and index-2 corrections.
errors: Self-acknowledged confusion at p. 594' between Z_{ρ,σ} and Z^!_{ρ,σ}; this page corrects it.
Notational inconsistency: (118) on the previous page writes N^*_ρ/μ, while (123) writes N^*_ρ/{±1}. These are the same since μ = {±1}.
Commutativity of the triangle (123) via the dashed arrow δ_Z is asserted or implied but not checked on this page.

ideas.what: Subgroups of the profinite automorphism group stabilizing the elliptic points ρ, σ are semidirect products (Galois-type group) ⋉ (procyclic inertia at the cusp), and are identified between the M_{1,1} and M_{0,3} settings.
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition groups at the cusp / tangential base point at infinity, inside GT-hat acting on profinite SL_2(Z) and on Γ_{0,4}/Γ_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura (decomposition groups at maximal degenerations); Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps and Nakamura–Schneps (GT-hat in genus 1)
ideas.where_published: Only hints of the M_{1,1}/M_{0,3} link appear in Esquisse d'un programme. The detailed computation is unpublished (Longue Marche continuation).

ideas.what: Index-2 inclusion ℓ_0 = ε_0^2 between the cusp loop in the π (free group) world and the 'half-loop' in the SL_2 (𝔊) world, inducing a morphism of extensions over the same Galois quotient.
ideas.modern_name: −1 ∈ SL_2 / half-twist at the cusp; SL_2 versus PSL_2 cusp stabilizers

ideas.what: Two 'canonical fundamental loops' a, b, projecting compatibly to γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ Π_Q^~ (diagram 123).
ideas.modern_name: Cocycles / paths between tangential base points in the GT-hat action (analogue of the f-component of GT elements)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld, Ihara (for GT); genus-1 analogues by Nakamura, Enriquez

missed.claim: This is an unpublished, explicit bookkeeping of cusp-inertia extensions in Grothendieck's own genus-0 versus genus-1 'équation des lacets' formalism, with a self-correction of an earlier confusion. It is mathematically close to later work on GT-hat in genus one, but gives no new result beyond that literature.
missed.quote: Il serait temps de rectifier la confusion (p. 594') entre Z = Z_{ρ,σ} ... et Z^! = Z^!_{ρ,σ}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is mainly of historical interest: it documents that Grothendieck worked out cusp decomposition-group structures linking M_{1,1} and M_{0,3} before the GT literature did.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly a notational correction and a routine index-2 comparison of semidirect-product extensions. The underlying ideas (cusp decomposition groups, the M_{1,1}/M_{0,3} comparison under GT-type groups) were later developed by others. Historically mildly interesting, with no new result visible on this page.
transcription_corrections: Top page number '649' is correct; the struck-out label at top-left is an earlier '(122)'/'(123)'.
(123) is a two-route diagram: Z^!_{ρ,σ} → N^*_ρ/{±1} →δ_ρ γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ Π_Q^~ above, Z^!_{ρ,σ} → N^*_σ →δ_σ γ_{ρ,σ} below, and the dashed δ_Z through the middle.
In the line before (124), the left-hand side is Z_{ρ,σ} with a crossed-out superscript, not Z^*.
Under ℓ_0 in (127) is written '‖ ε_0^{2Ẑ}', i.e. ℓ_0^{Ẑ} = ε_0^{2Ẑ}.

Last line reads roughly: 'Bien entendu, c'est dire[?] sur Z^!_{ρ,σ}, non sur Z_{ρ,σ}, qu'on a défini (117), (118) d'où (123)'. The point is that (117)–(118) and hence (123) are defined on Z^!, not on Z.
